daily.title: Pakistan-Taliban conflict: How India could benefit from shifting regional dynamics
daily.summary: As Pakistan's influence in Afghanistan comes under strain, India is rebuilding ties with the Taliban in Kabul. Can New Delhi turn this diplomatic opening into lasting strategic gains?

daily.title: Russia frees jailed American Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff talks
daily.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American taken captive by Russian forces years ago in Ukraine.

daily.title: UK approves Jackdaw gas field after years in limbo
daily.summary: Drilling is set to begin in the controversial North Sea plot as the government seeks to tackle high energy costs. Environmental groups have criticized the move and called for more clean energy.

daily.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
daily.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

daily.title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs after car attack as suspect appears in court
daily.summary: Doctors have amputated both of Helen Haines legs after the Australian lawmaker was hit in an apparent deliberate attack. The suspected driver involved in the attack has appeared in court.

daily.title: Germany news: 'Tech error' brings early cigarette tax hike
daily.summary: Germany's Finance Ministry has said the tax hike went into effect months early due to a "technical error." AfD co-Chair Alice Weidel will present "A New Deal for Europe" in Strasbourg. Follow DW for the latest.

daily.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
daily.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

daily.title: India news: India-US trade deal 'pretty close,' says Trump
daily.summary: US President Donald Trump hinted that the US-India trade deal could look different from the previous ones. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: Musk says SpaceX-Tesla merger 'good idea' as companies explore union
daily.summary: Musk confirmed the long standing speculation of a possible merger between Tesla and SpaceX but warned that it would be premature to assume it is happening for sure.

daily.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
daily.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

daily.title: Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink in Ukraine — report
daily.summary: Elon Musk "capped the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network," the Wall Street Journal reported.

daily.title: UK fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
daily.summary: The UK is sending military support to Saudi Arabia as Iran-aligned Houthi rebels launch repeated attacks on the kingdom.

daily.title: Portugal housing protests continue after police clear camps
daily.summary: Demonstrators vow to continue their campaign to call for affordable housing in Portugal after police cleared tent camps and arrested at least 55 people.

daily.title: AfD's Alice Weidel to unveil plan to cut EU powers — report
daily.summary: The far-right AfD will propose slashing powers of the European Union when it presents its policy paper on Wednesday, Politico reports.

daily.title: Zelenskyy visits Norway amid Trump White House tensions
daily.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy met with Norwegian and Finnish leaders in Oslo and held talks with Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Trump is pressuring Zelenskyy to "make a deal" with Russia.

daily.title: Nigeria records its first Ebola case, in capital Abuja
daily.summary: Nigeria has reported its first known case of Ebola during Africa's latest outbreak originating in the DRC. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate said the patient was a woman who had recently flown to Abuja from Uganda.

daily.title: Lebanon faces uncertainty as UNIFIL mandate nears end
daily.summary: As UN peacekeeping forces prepare to withdraw from Lebanon, Israel remains present and Hezbollah is still armed. A new EU support mission aims to strengthen Lebanon's army, but will not replace UN peacekeepers.

daily.title: Sudan drone strike kills around 150 in Abyei market
daily.summary: A drone strike hit a market in the Abyei border region disputed by Sudan and South Sudan and killed dozens. The drone caused a large fire when it hit a fuel depot. South Sudanese officials blamed Sudan's military.

daily.title: North Korean workers treated as 'slaves' at Russian drone factory
daily.summary: A new report reveals the plight of North Korean workers at a drone factory in Russia. It also raised concerns that Pyongyang could gain hands-on knowledge of advanced weapons systems through the workers it sends there.

daily.title: New EU plan for Arctic warily eyes influence of Russia, US
daily.summary: The EU unveiled its priorities in the Arctic as it vies with Russia, China and the US for influence. EU foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said drone incursions, GPS jamming and cable sabotage undermine Arctic security.

daily.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
daily.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

daily.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
daily.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

weekly.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
weekly.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

weekly.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
weekly.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

weekly.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
weekly.summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

weekly.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
weekly.summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

weekly.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
weekly.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

weekly.title: What Earth's sixth mass extinction event means for humans
weekly.summary: Human activity is driving plants and animals to extinction at an unprecedented rate. As countries meet in Armenia to discuss ways to reverse nature loss, DW reveals how declining biodiversity is already harming people.

weekly.title: France: Young voters blase about Glucksmann's Socialists
weekly.summary: Raphael Glucksmann wants to lead France's Socialists to power without working with the left-populist Jean-Luc Melenchon, who is particularly popular with young voters. How can the center-left candidate win them over?

weekly.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
weekly.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

weekly.title: How reliant is Ukraine on the US-controlled Starlink internet service?
weekly.summary: Kyiv keeps issuing warnings that the satellite internet system Starlink is being restricted in Ukraine. How dependent is the country on the system, and what would happen if it went down?

weekly.title: Populist Czech PM Babis goes empty-handed in Senate elections
weekly.summary: Opposition parties still control the Czech Senate, in a major blow to Prime Minister Andrej Babis' and his governing coalition.

weekly.title: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
weekly.summary: Experts believe that, so far, Germany has been ill-prepared — both militarily and mentally — for Russian provocations. They also warn against the idea that ending support for Ukraine would make Germany safer.

weekly.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
weekly.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

weekly.title: Russia wants blackout in Ukraine as winter comes — Zelenskyy
weekly.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy says Russia is trying to cut electricity and heating to civilians ahead of winter. He also called the US president's waiver of new sanctions on Moscow a boost for Vladimir Putin.

weekly.title: France: Protesters clash with police in nationwide protests, amid rising social polarization
weekly.summary: Unrest broke out in parts of France as students, trade unionists and Yellow Vest activists took to the streets to protest high prices and inequality. Police arrested over 1,000 people amid chaotic scenes.

weekly.title: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
weekly.summary: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine at the Brussels summit. But souring relations with the US over Russia and Starlink and a big hole in the budget will make for a difficult winter for Ukraine.

weekly.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?
weekly.summary: Girls wearing headscarves have been turned away from schools in Azerbaijan, triggering unusual protests involving children. The government rules do not mention hijabs. Why are schools enforcing unwritten rules?

weekly.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
weekly.summary: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

weekly.title: Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
weekly.summary: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

weekly.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
weekly.summary: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

weekly.title: Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
weekly.summary: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

weekly.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
weekly.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

weekly.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
weekly.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

weekly.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
weekly.summary: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

weekly.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
weekly.summary: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

weekly.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
weekly.summary: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

weekly.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
weekly.summary: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

weekly.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
weekly.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

weekly.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
weekly.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

weekly.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
weekly.summary: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

weekly.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
weekly.summary: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

weekly.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
weekly.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

weekly.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
weekly.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

weekly.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
weekly.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

weekly.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
weekly.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

weekly.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
weekly.summary: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?

weekly.title: Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
weekly.summary: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

weekly.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
weekly.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

weekly.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
weekly.summary: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
